docs.title: Star Org Labs
docs.text:
Run your Star Citizen org like a pro — from Discord to a full web command center. Events, fleet, loot, mining, and org ops in one connected system.

Open the app → Get started

docs.title: Why Star Org Labs?
docs.text:
Running an org is a second job — scheduling ops, chasing signups, tracking who actually showed, splitting loot fairly, keeping the fleet and treasury straight. Star Org Labs pulls all of it into one connected system so you spend less time on spreadsheets and more time flying.

  • Events & Operations

    Plan an op in minutes with a guided event wizard. Members sign up for roles and ships in Discord, you reuse templates for regular runs, track attendance & reliability over time, and settle the haul with the built-in Loot Hub.

  • Fleet & Hangar

    Every member gets a Personal Hangar to register their ships, and leadership gets an Org Fleet Dashboard to see exactly what the org can field.

  • Org Command

    A home base for leadership: member & server dashboards, personnel roster, org structure, a recruitment hub, support tickets, goals, guild points, treasury, and a public website CMS.

  • Industrial

    Tools for the working fleet: mining sessions, a cargo optimizer, the RSIG decoder, a rock calculator, and work orders.

  • Make it yours

    Theme the whole portal to your manufacturer of choice — Aegis, Drake, Origin, RSI, MISC, and more — or set an org-wide look for your members.

  • Lives in Discord

    Signups, reminders, and pings happen right where your members already are. Your leadership commands from the web; your members never leave chat.

docs.title: Discord Commands
docs.text:
Star Org Labs lives right in your server. Type / in any channel and Discord shows you the bot's commands — but you'll rarely need to memorize them. Most of the action happens through buttons on the event posts. This page is your cheat sheet for when you do want to type.

!!! info "Who can run what" - Everyone — no badge. - Officer — event and loot organizers. - Admin — server owners / configuration.

Officer and Admin are set up by your server's leadership in **Server Settings**. Servers
using **Advanced permissions** can also grant or restrict whole modules per rank — see
[Roles & Permissions](permissions.md). A member whose rank lacks a module still sees its
commands; running one answers privately that their rank doesn't have access.

Every command runs **inside a server** — none of them work in a DM with the bot.

docs.title: 🎮 Joining the action
docs.text:
Everything you need to show up and fly.

Command What it does /events See every upcoming op in your org. /event <id> Open a specific event — with buttons to sign up, pick a role, and choose your ship. /join_event <id> Jump straight into an event. /bring_ship <id> Sign up and bring one of your ships to the fight. /rsi verify <handle> Link and verify your RSI handle so your org knows who you are in the 'verse. /timezone <zone> Set your timezone (e.g. America/New_York) so event times show correctly for you.

You mostly just click

Once an event is posted, signing up, choosing a role, and picking a ship all happen with buttons and menus right on the event. /events is usually all you need to type.

docs.title: Your RSI accounts — /rsi
docs.text:
You can link more than one RSI handle (e.g. a main and an alt) and pick which is your main.

Command What it does /rsi verify <handle> Link and verify an RSI handle to your profile. /rsi list See every RSI handle you've linked. /rsi set_main <handle> Choose which linked handle is your main. /rsi unlink <handle> Remove a linked handle.

Renamed: /rsi set_main was /rsi set-main up to and including 1.0.0-beta.196. If it doesn't autocomplete, type the underscore version — every other command on the bot is snake_case, and this was the odd one out.

These four work in a DM with the bot as well as in a server: they only ever touch your own account.

docs.title: 🚀 Your fleet & mates
docs.text: Command What it does /fleet status See your fleet and your mates. /fleet add_mate <member> Add someone as a mate in your fleet. /fleet remove_mate <member> Remove a mate.

docs.title: ⛏️ Mining & industry
docs.text:
Available when your server has Mining Tools turned on.

Command What it does /mining start Kick off a mining session for this channel — the bot posts a thread for it; track yields and crew on the web. /mining materials Check current material prices and stats (instability, resistance, and more). /mining rock <signature> [laser_power] Decode an RSIG signature or radar ping — mass, composition, and (with laser power) whether you can crack it.

docs.title: 🎯 Goals & giving back
docs.text: Command What it does /goal pledge <goal_id> <item> <amount> Contribute materials toward one of your org's goals. /ticket create [category] Open a support ticket with your leadership. /ticket close Close your ticket when it's sorted. /boosts See your Patreon boost slots and the servers you sponsor. /guild boost Spend a boost slot to support this server (raises its capacity). /guild unboost Reclaim a boost slot to use somewhere else.

docs.title: Running ops (Officers)
docs.text:
Organize events, templates, recurring runs, and loot.

EventsRecurring eventsLoot Hub Command What it does /create_event <template> <title> [date] [time] Launch an op from a saved template. Defaults to today at 20:00 UTC. /delete_event <id> Cancel an event (notifies signups, cleans up channels). /move_event_crew <id> Pull all confirmed attendees into your voice channel. /start_op <id> Ping/DM signed-up members who aren't in voice yet to join your channel. /refresh_event_embed <id> Repost the event to the top of the channel. /create_vcs <id> Create temp voice channels for the event's teams that don't have one yet. /templates List your event templates. /create_template <name> [description] Start a new template, then build it out with buttons. /poll create [title] Post an availability poll to find the best time. Command What it does /recurring list See your recurring schedules. /recurring create <name> <cron> [days] Auto-post an event on a schedule (e.g. every Friday night). /recurring add_template <id> <template> Attach a template to a schedule. /recurring toggle_roulette <id> Randomize which template runs each time. /recurring toggle_active <id> Pause or resume a schedule. /recurring toggle_poll <id> Let members vote on the next mission — votes weight the roulette, and an officer confirms the winner. /recurring polls See the active mission polls and their vote tallies. /recurring skip_next <id> Take one night off. The schedule keeps running after it. /recurring unskip_next <id> Changed your mind — put that night back on. /recurring one_off <name> <templates> <date> <time> Run a one-off roulette for a single night, with no schedule attached. Command What it does /loot create <name> [event] [points] [sync_vc] Start a loot session. sync_vc adds everyone in your voice channel. /loot roll <session> Run the fair, weighted roll. /loot next_round <session> [points] Move to the next round and top up points. /wheel <names> [mode] Spin a quick wheel for a random winner — great for giveaways. /goal create_template <template> <qty> Set an org goal from a Wikelo preset. /goal create_custom <name> <reward> <reqs> <qty> Create a fully custom org goal.

docs.title: Setting up the server (Admins)
docs.text:
Command What it does /setup Quickly create the basic channels and roles the bot needs. Discord shows it to members with Manage Server; if your Admin role doesn't have that permission, grant it the command in Server Settings → Integrations. /settings view Review the current configuration at a glance. /settings set_officer_role <role> Choose which Discord role grants Officer powers. /settings set_admin_role <role> Choose which Discord role grants Admin powers. /settings officers List everyone who currently has Officer powers. /settings set_uex_key Add your UEXCorp API key for live market data (typed into a private pop-up). /ticket category list See the ticket categories members can open tickets under. /ticket category add <name> Add a ticket category (plus optional manager role, auto-close days, and auto-assign role). /ticket category edit <name> Rename a category or change its roles and auto-close days. /ticket category remove <name> Delete a category once it has no tickets left. /guild status See the server's pooled capacity and who's sponsoring it. /permission Check that the bot has all the permissions it needs here.

Something not working?

If a command doesn't appear, your server may not have that feature enabled, or you may need Officer/Admin. Ask your leadership — or drop into the Star Org Labs community and we'll help you out.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Get your org up and running in a few minutes — no installs, no spreadsheets.

docs.title: 1. Open the app & sign in
docs.text: Head to starorg.tools and sign in with Discord. Star Org Labs uses your Discord account, so there's nothing new to create.

docs.title: 2. Add the bot to your server
docs.text: In the app, use "Add to Server" and pick the Discord server you want to run your org from. You'll need permission to add a bot to that server.

docs.title: 3. Set up your org
docs.text:
From Server Settings, make it yours:

  • Drop in your org logo
  • Pick a theme — your manufacturer's colors, or a look of your own
  • Configure your channels so events and pings land in the right place
  • Map your officer and admin roles — and see Roles & Permissions for per-rank access control

docs.title: 4. Run your first op
docs.text: Hit Create Event, build out the roster (roles, ships, teams), and share it. Your members sign up straight from Discord — and you track it all from the web. 🎉

docs.title: What's next?
docs.text:
Explore from the sidebar

  • Events & Ops — templates, recurring events, attendance, the Loot Hub
  • Org Command — roster, structure, recruitment, goals, treasury
  • Industrial — mining sessions, cargo optimizer, work orders

Want the full list of what you can type? See the Discord Commands cheat sheet. More detailed guides — event planning, loot distribution — are on the way. Have a question in the meantime? Ask in the Star Org Labs community.

docs.title: Roles & Permissions
docs.text: Who can do what in your org — and how to customize it.

docs.title: The basics
docs.text:
Every server starts in Basic mode with three tiers:

Tier Who What they can do Member Everyone in your org Join events, use the loot hub, industry tools, voice tools, track their own career Officer Your event & loot organizers Everything members can, plus the staff surfaces — tickets, treasury, roster, recruitment, attendance, fleet dashboard, org chart Admin Server owners / leadership Everything, including Server Settings and the public website CMS

Officer and Admin are mapped from your Discord roles in Server Settings → Core → Access & Roles. Members with Discord's Manage Server or Administrator permission count automatically.

docs.title: Advanced mode: permissions per rank
docs.text:
Bigger orgs often want more nuance than three tiers — a Logistics rank that can view the treasury, or a probationary rank that can't open loot sessions yet. That's Advanced mode:

  • Every rank in your org chart gets its own set of feature toggles, managed in a matrix on Server Settings → Permissions.
  • Members with no rank have their own pinned row in the matrix, so nobody falls through the cracks.
  • Grants work both ways: you can open staff surfaces (like the treasury view) to a trusted rank, or restrict member surfaces (like events) from one.
  • Management can be delegated too: the Events Management and Loot Management toggles let a rank run recurring schedules, roulette, and loot sessions without making them full officers.

You can't lock yourself out

Officers and admins always keep their tier's access, whatever the matrix says. Rank toggles only affect regular members — and switching back to Basic instantly restores the classic ladder, keeping your grants saved for later.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text: Advanced mode is rolling out gradually. When it's enabled for your server, the switch lives in Server Settings → Core → Access & Roles; flipping it seeds every rank with normal member access, so nothing changes until you start customizing. If the switch tells you it isn't enabled yet, reach out on the support Discord.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Ranks themselves are created and ordered in Org Chart — the Permissions matrix only decides what each rank can use.
  • Deleting a rank discards its toggles; its members follow the "Unranked members" row until they're re-ranked.
  • In Discord, a member whose rank lacks a module can still see its slash commands — running one just answers privately that their rank doesn't have access.
